title: Validate onboarding step: track “Visited usage dashboard” in Console (privacy-safe)
creator: Marissa Cole
content:
## Summary
Implement client-side validation for the guided onboarding checklist step “Visited usage dashboard”. When a user (in an eligible org/project) navigates to the Usage dashboard in the Redwood Console, we should:
1) emit an onboarding telemetry event (privacy-safe)
2) mark the checklist step complete via the checklist state API (idempotent)

This is a Phase 1 step for Hosted API onboarding.

## Background / Why
During beta, we want to know whether new users are discovering usage analytics (tokens/cost/latency) early. It’s also a strong predictor of readiness for production and reduces support load (e.g., debugging 429s / unexpected spend).

This step must be client-side because “dashboard visit” is a Console navigation action rather than a gateway event.

## Requirements
### Functional
- Detect when a user has visited the Usage dashboard page in Console (SPA navigation).
- Only count the visit when the Usage dashboard is actually rendered (not just route prefetch).
- Mark checklist step complete at most once per project.
- Emit telemetry event per schema v1, with dedupe/idempotency.
- Must work for:
  - direct deep link to usage page
  - navigation via sidebar
  - browser back/forward
  - refresh on the usage route

### Privacy / Security constraints
Follow Confluence: `architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/onboarding-telemetry-event-schema-v1` and security review constraints (no customer prompt content, allowlisted properties only).
- Do NOT include:
  - full URL (may contain query params with customer identifiers)
  - report filters that may include customer IDs (e.g., `user_id`, `email`, free-form labels)
  - anything derived from prompts or request payloads
- Do include only allowlisted identifiers:
  - `org_id` (internal UUID)
  - `project_id` (internal UUID)
  - `actor_id` (internal user ID)
  - `session_id` (client generated)
  - `source = console`
  - `step_id = usage_dashboard_visit`
  - `route_name = usage_dashboard` (enum)

If we need more properties, they must be added to the allowlist via ENG-23120.

## Proposed implementation
### Route detection
- Hook into the Console router (React Router) in the Usage dashboard top-level page component.
- On first mount of Usage dashboard page component, schedule a completion attempt.

### “Actually visited” signal
To avoid counting accidental/transient navigations, require one of:
- page stays mounted for >= 2 seconds, OR
- at least one usage API call completes successfully (preferred)

Preferred approach: mark complete when we get a successful response from the usage summary endpoint that the page already calls (e.g., `/console/api/usage/summary`). This is both more accurate and avoids issues with people navigating away immediately.

### Checklist completion write
- Call checklist state update endpoint from ENG-23111 (server-side state):
  - `POST /console/api/onboarding/checklist/steps/complete` (exact path may differ; use the new client wrapper)
  - Include `project_id` + `step_id`.
- Idempotency:
  - include `dedupe_key = <project_id>:usage_dashboard_visit`
  - server should treat as upsert; client should tolerate 409/200 either way
- Ensure this is gated behind the guided onboarding feature flag (ENG-23118 rollout logic). If flag is off, do not emit event and do not write state.

### Telemetry
Emit `onboarding.step_completed` (or the agreed name in schema) with properties:
- `step_id: usage_dashboard_visit`
- `step_group: observability` (if allowlisted)
- `completion_method: client_validated`
- `route_name: usage_dashboard`
- `dedupe_key`

Important: do not attach the full URL; only use the route enum.

### Edge cases
- Multi-project org: completion must be per project. Use the current project context.
- If project context is missing (rare), do nothing and log a debug-only warning.
- If usage APIs 403 due to permissions, do not mark complete; still okay to emit `onboarding.step_viewed` (if schema supports) but do not invent new events without schema signoff.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Visiting Usage dashboard and successfully loading usage data marks “Visited usage dashboard” complete in checklist UI within 5 seconds.
- [ ] Step remains complete after refresh and across sessions (server state).
- [ ] Telemetry event emitted exactly once per project (dedupe enforced).
- [ ] No URL, query params, or filter values sent in telemetry payload.
- [ ] Behind feature flag; no changes for non-eligible cohorts.
- [ ] Unit test for the completion trigger logic + basic integration test stub (E2E coverage is tracked in ENG-23124).

## Notes / Links
- PRD: `confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-checklist-prd-2026-01`
- UX spec: `confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-guided-onboarding-ux-spec-2026-01`
- Telemetry schema v1: `confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/onboarding-telemetry-event-schema-v1`
- Privacy review: `confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/onboarding-telemetry-privacy-review`

## Implementation plan
1) Add `useOnboardingStepCompletion(step_id)` helper to consolidate dedupe + flag gating (if not already created in ENG-23112).
2) In Usage dashboard page component, wire completion to successful usage summary fetch.
3) Emit telemetry event via standard client telemetry emitter with allowlisted properties only.
4) Add unit tests for “completion after successful fetch” + “no completion when flag off”.

## Open questions
- Confirm event name with Nadia (schema owner): `onboarding.step_completed` vs `onboarding_checklist.step_completed`.
- Confirm whether we want a separate `step_viewed` event for funnel diagnostics, and whether it’s already in schema.

---

## Activity / comments
### 2026-02-10 (Hannah Rivera)
I’m going to tie completion to the existing usage summary fetch. Timing-based completion (2s mount) is less reliable for fast nav/back. This also prevents marking complete when the user can’t load usage due to permissions.

### 2026-02-12 (Nadia Rahman)
Please do not send any URL/path. `route_name` as enum is OK. Keep payload minimal; anything not in the allowlist will be dropped by the privacy filter.

### 2026-02-15 (Marcus Lin)
Privacy note: usage filters can contain user-provided strings. Make sure we don’t attach any filter state to the event. Also ensure `actor_id` comes from internal auth context, not email.

### 2026-02-18 (Hannah Rivera)
Patch up in branch. Using `dedupe_key = ${projectId}:usage_dashboard_visit`. Also added guard: if `projectId` missing, return early. Requesting review from Dylan + Nadia.

### 2026-02-21 (Dylan Brooks)
Looks good. One request: ensure we don’t fire completion on cached responses before the component is mounted (some of our data hooks can resolve immediately). Add a `hasMountedRef` to prevent weird double-fires. Approving once addressed.
